---
name: Code Quality Monitoring

on:
  schedule: weekly on monday
  workflow_dispatch: {}
  # A weekly agent with nothing new to say would otherwise reopen the same
  # findings forever; hold off while any of its issues is still unaddressed.
  skip-if-match: 'is:issue is:open in:title "[quality] "'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read

# OpenRouter has no first-class engine; it is reached by pointing the claude
# engine's base URL at it. gh-aw sees a custom endpoint and stops rewriting the
# model slug, so the provider-prefixed name passes through intact.
engine:
  id: claude
  env:
    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5

# The agent runs behind the AWF egress firewall, so the provider host has to be
# allowlisted explicitly.
network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - openrouter.ai

# Sonnet 5's list price. The AWF proxy rejects models missing from its built-in
# pricing table with HTTP 400, and a provider-prefixed slug is not in it.
models:
  default-ai-credits-pricing:
    input: 3
    output: 15

timeout-minutes: 20

# The agent runs inside the AWF sandbox, which mounts the workspace but not
# /nix -- so the linters cannot run from the agent's bash. They run here, on
# the host, and reach the agent through the workspace. `--inputs-from .` pins
# them to the same nixpkgs the flake itself builds against.
steps:
  - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v30
    with:
      extra_nix_config: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes

  # statix has no substitute in cache.nixos.org and builds from source, dragging
  # in the whole Rust toolchain. Same cache the CI workflow uses, same reason.
  - uses: DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action@v14
    with:
      use-flakehub: false

  - name: Install the linters
    run: |
      nix profile install --inputs-from . \
        nixpkgs#statix nixpkgs#deadnix nixpkgs#nixfmt \
        nixpkgs#ruff nixpkgs#shellcheck

  - name: Collect linter reports
    run: |
      mkdir -p .quality-reports
      # Every linter here exits non-zero on findings, and Actions runs this
      # under `bash -e`. The `if` suspends errexit so one tool's findings do
      # not abort the tools after it.
      record() {
        report=".quality-reports/$1.txt"
        shift
        printf '$ %s\n\n' "$*" > "$report"
        if "$@" >> "$report" 2>&1; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
        printf '\nexit=%s\n' "$status" >> "$report"
      }

      # errfmt over statix's default: no ANSI escapes, one finding per line.
      record statix    statix check --format errfmt .
      record deadnix   deadnix --fail .
      # nixfmt deprecated directory arguments; feed it the tracked files.
      record nixfmt    nixfmt --check $(git ls-files '*.nix')
      record ruff      ruff check pkgs/claude-session-registry
      record shellcheck shellcheck scripts/bootstrap-macos.sh

# No `github:` tool — the checks below read the local checkout, so the agent
# needs no GitHub API access beyond the issues it files via safe-outputs.
tools:
  bash: ["*"]

safe-outputs:
  create-issue:
    title-prefix: "[quality] "
    labels: [code-quality, automation]
    max: 5
---

# Weekly Code Quality Review

This repository is a Home Manager flake that configures macOS (aarch64) and
Linux workstations. It is mostly Nix, plus two Python scripts and one bootstrap
shell script.

Read `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` first — they define the conventions this review
is meant to enforce.

Nix is **not** available to you. The linters have already run; their output is
in `.quality-reports/`, one file per tool, each ending in the tool's exit code:

| Report | Tool | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `statix.txt` | statix | Nix anti-patterns |
| `deadnix.txt` | deadnix | Unused Nix bindings |
| `nixfmt.txt` | nixfmt | Nix formatting |
| `ruff.txt` | ruff | `pkgs/claude-session-registry/*.py` |
| `shellcheck.txt` | shellcheck | `scripts/bootstrap-macos.sh` |

`.quality-reports/` is generated by this workflow and is not part of the
repository — never report it as a finding.

A non-zero `exit=` on its own is normal — every one of these tools exits
non-zero when it finds something. Judge a report by body and exit code
together:

- Findings in the body, non-zero exit — the normal case. Review them.
- Empty body, `exit=0` — the tool ran and found nothing. Clean.
- An error about the tool itself rather than about the code — `command not
  found`, `exit=127`, an evaluation or panic message — means the check never
  ran. Both streams are captured, so this is always visible in the body.

File that last case as a **High** severity issue and say which checks were
therefore not performed. A review that silently skipped half its checks is
worse than no review.

## What to Analyze

1. **The linter reports.** Group what they found by cause, not by file.
   Prioritize `statix` anti-patterns and `deadnix` unused bindings over
   formatting noise.

2. **`pkgs/claude-session-registry/restore.py`** is over 500 lines. If `ruff`
   also reports complexity or duplication there, name the responsibilities that
   could be split out — do not simply quote the line count.

3. **README drift.** `CLAUDE.md` requires the "Managed packages" section of
   `README.md` to stay in sync with the packages installed by `home/home.nix`.
   Compare the two and report packages present in one but missing from the
   other, and `macOS` / `Linux` tags that no longer match the platform
   conditionals in `home/home.nix`.

4. **Flake input staleness.** Read the `lastModified` timestamps in
   `flake.lock` and flag any input not updated in more than 90 days, naming the
   input and its age.

## What to Create

Create **one issue per finding category**, not one per file. Each issue should
name the affected files with `path:line` references, explain why the finding
matters for this repository specifically, suggest a concrete first step, and
assign a severity: High for anything that can break activation on a fresh
machine, Medium for maintainability, Low for style. Skip a category with fewer
than 3 instances unless at least one of them is High.

If every report is clean and nothing above turns up, create no issues at all.

## What to Skip

- Anything CI already catches. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `nix flake check`,
  builds the activation package on both platforms, and smoke-tests activation and
  the interactive-zsh PATH. A finding that would turn CI red is not a finding.
- Formatting-only issues when `nixfmt.txt` is clean.
- Style preferences with no linter rule behind them.
- Pinned version and hash literals in `pkgs/*-darwin/default.nix`. Those track
  upstream DMG releases and are expected to lag; bumping them is a separate,
  manual job.
- Suggestions to add tooling the repository has deliberately rejected — check
  `README.md` "Notes" and the git history before proposing a new dependency.
